My take:
I think they are both tough, but probably the latter is tougher. Here’s why:
First, everyone knows a new VP of Sales has some time to figure things out after she joins. They know there will be a dip, even if they don’t expect it. before: There are many issues with the VP of Sales hires we all make -- and I'm guilty here myself. We hire folks too quickly sometimes (e.g., a month) when we need someone now. And we often hire VPs of Sales without checking if they can really sell themselves. But one thing you'll hear me talk about again and again is how important it is for your VP of Sales to start closing deals on Day 1. That's what matters most. If nothing else changes after they join. So maybe don't worry so much about the fact that no new reps were hired under this VP of Sales before Month 3. Or even Month 6. Instead, just watch what happens to closed-won revenue under her / him.
